clue.text: Drop it to break the Pythian seat

indicators.note: breaking the two words apart and resetting them signals that their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to let something fall so as to smash the priestess's chair at Delphi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' rearranges the six letters of DROP IT. The Pythia, Apollo's priestess at Delphi, gave her oracles seated on a three-legged stool.
explanation.definitionFit: The Delphic oracle's priestess famously sat on a three-legged stand, so her seat is this object.

clue.text: Game of chance that is, in a way, allowed

indicators.note: in places the word for allowed inside the word for a way

parts.note: a route is a way or path
let means permitted

explanation.surface: A gambling game is said to be legal in a certain manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is 'in'. 'that is' is only a link between the definition and the wordplay, not part of either.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino gambling game played with a spinning wheel and ball.

clue.text: Book of maxims

parts.note: the Old Testament book of wise sayings attributed to Solomon

explanation.surface: A collection of wise sayings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament book of sayings attributed to Solomon is named for its short wise saws.

clue.text: He works on what you're reading

definitions.text: He works on what you're reading

parts.words: He works on what you're reading
parts.note: you are reading clues, and an investigator works on clues; also the hero of a crime novel you might be reading

explanation.surface: A comment about someone busy with the very page in front of you.
explanation.walkthrough: What you are reading is clues, and solving clues is an investigator's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth investigates crimes by following clues, which is what the solver reads.

clue.text: Such customers being well fitted at the tailor's

definitions.text: Such customers being well fitted at the tailor's

parts.words: Such customers being well fitted at the tailor's
parts.note: a tailor's client who can be fitted with a suit could jokingly be called ..., which is also the ordinary word for fitting

explanation.surface: A remark about clients getting a good fit when they visit the tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The everyday adjective meaning appropriate is read as 'able to be suited', which is what a tailor's customer wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Read in two halves the adjective means capable of being clothed in a suit, while its usual sense is appropriate or well fitted.

clue.text: This show should contain some hit numbers

definitions.text: This show should contain some hit numbers

parts.words: This show should contain some hit numbers
parts.note: hit numbers suggests chart successes, but means routines with people being struck, as in knockabout farce

explanation.surface: A remark that a stage show needs some popular songs.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hit number' is a popular song, but here it is a routine where performers hit each other, as in knockabout farce.
explanation.definitionFit: Knockabout comedy built on pratfalls and blows, named after a clown's paddle that makes a loud smack.

clue.text: Holdings for a number by a devious ruse

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: devious means winding or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Property is obtained by a numbers trick and a crafty ploy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' rearranges the letters of 'ruse' to give URES; 'by' and 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenancy periods or terms of landholding are holdings of property or office.

clue.text: Good French is about right this side of the Channel

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the French word goes around the other piece

parts.note: bon is French for good
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something good in French is said to be correct on the English side of the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is 'about'. The definition is a resort on England's south coast, across the English Channel from France.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-coast English seaside resort lies on the English side of the sea that separates Britain from France.

clue.text: One does one's level best to ensure it

definitions.text: One does one's level best to ensure it

parts.words: One does one's level best to ensure it
parts.note: doing one's level best means trying hard, but here it is taken literally as working to make something flat and level

explanation.surface: Someone tries as hard as they can to guarantee something.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'do one's level best' means try hard; read literally, levelling achieves flatness and uniformity.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatness or uniformity is what levelling achieves.

clue.text: Popular drink? Not with me if not mine

definitions.text: Popular drink? Not with me if not mine

parts.words: Popular drink? Not with me if not mine
parts.note: the national hot beverage, and the idiom 'not my ...' for something one does not care for: if it is not to my taste, it is not with me

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a well-loved drink unless it is their own.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'not my cup of tea' means something you do not like, so if it is not yours you will not have it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewed mug of the British staple beverage is popular, and the idiom describes what one personally likes.

clue.text: Whole tree in ruins

indicators.note: something in ruins is wrecked and rebuilt in another shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An entire tree lies wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins' rearranges TREE and IN together; 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete and undivided are synonyms of the adjective whole.

clue.text: Changes to open-field farming with earthworks?

definitions.text: Changes to open-field farming with earthworks?

parts.words: Changes to open-field farming with earthworks?
parts.note: read as ..., the removal of hedges and fences on farmland, while the real sense is fortifications such as ramparts and earthworks

explanation.surface: A question about how open-field agriculture was altered by digging banks.
explanation.walkthrough: Open-field farming had no fences; the word for military fortifications can be read as 'de-fences', taking fences away.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthworks such as ramparts and ditches are fortifications that protect a position, the plural noun's usual sense.

clue.text: Arab in a street has a Chaldean feature

parts.note: Ur was a city of the Chaldees, the biblical home of Abraham
a chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: An Arab in the street is said to have a face like the ancient Chaldeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Street Arab' is an old term for a homeless child roaming the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A street Arab was a dated term for a ragged child living on the streets, an urchin by another name.

clue.text: Theirs may be a distressing job

definitions.text: Theirs may be a distressing job

parts.words: Theirs may be a distressing job
parts.note: distress in law means seizing goods for unpaid debts, so the officers who carry out distraint have a job that is distressing in both senses

explanation.surface: A sympathetic remark about people whose work is upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: Distress (distraint) is the legal seizure of goods to pay a debt, carried out by these court officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Court officers who seize property for debts perform distraint, legally called distress.

clue.text: It helps to maintain a high standard

definitions.text: It helps to maintain a high standard

parts.words: It helps to maintain a high standard
parts.note: a high standard sounds like quality, but a standard is a flag, held high on a pole

explanation.surface: A remark about something that helps keep quality up.
explanation.walkthrough: A standard is also a flag, and this pole keeps it flying high.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner, and the pole it flies from holds it aloft.

clue.text: Confusion where army rations are consumed

definitions.meaning: the room where soldiers or officers eat together

explanation.surface: Chaos at mealtime in the army canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A muddle is a synonym, and the military dining hall shares the same word.

clue.text: They're sent to girls about four

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for girls goes around the numeral

parts.note: misses are girls or young women
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Some items are posted to young women, around four of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is 'about'. 'to' is a link word, and 'They're sent' is the definition, read as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters or written messages are things dispatched to someone.

clue.text: Lots get knocked down here

parts.note: lots suggests a great deal, but means items for sale, knocked down by the auctioneer's hammer

explanation.surface: A place where much gets demolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' are auction items, and the auctioneer 'knocks them down' to the highest bidder with the gavel.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction house's room is where items are sold under the hammer.

clue.text: They are extremely objective

parts.note: the plural noun means both extremities, the points at the far edges, and aims or objectives

explanation.surface: A comment on people who are utterly impartial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' points to extremities, and 'objective' to goals; the plural noun means both.
explanation.definitionFit: The far tips of something are its extremities, and the same plural noun means aims or goals.

clue.text: One result of training in arboriculture

definitions.text: One result of training in arboriculture

parts.words: One result of training in arboriculture
parts.note: training here is guiding the branches of a fruit tree along a frame or wall, not instructing people

explanation.surface: An outcome of a course in tree-growing.
explanation.walkthrough: Training a tree means tying its branches flat to a wall or trellis.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit tree whose branches are trained flat against a wall or lattice.

clue.text: Dentists on the square ?

parts.note: people who drill teeth, and soldiers drilling on the parade square

explanation.surface: A question about dental practitioners in a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: Dentists drill teeth; drill is also marching practice on a parade square.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentists bore teeth with a drill, and soldiers practise drill on the parade ground.

clue.text: Feeble bewilderment, say, when we have to work

indicators.note: say asks the solver to speak the words and hear another pair

parts.note: feeble is weak and bewilderment is a daze

explanation.surface: A dazed, helpless feeling at the thought of a working week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the sound signal: WEAK DAZE spoken out loud gives the working days of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Monday to Friday are the days of the week on which most people are employed.

clue.text: This state gives few real change

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters

explanation.surface: A government is said to make little real difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges FEW and REAL. 'This state' points to the welfare state, which gives benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase welfare state names a nation providing social benefits, so this word fills in for the state.

clue.text: Does she come out at night ?

definitions.text: Does she come out at night ?

parts.words: Does she come out at night ?
parts.note: a woman's name that is also the Latin for a star, which appears after dark

explanation.surface: A question about a woman who goes out in the evenings.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl's name is Latin for star, which 'comes out at night'.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name meaning star in Latin, and stars appear in the night sky.

clue.text: Twisted cables to make a road-block perhaps

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tangled cables form a barrier across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' rearranges CABLES and TO together; 'perhaps' marks a roadblock as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadblock is one kind of barrier or hindrance in the way.

clue.text: Blooming good instruments

parts.note: blooming reads as an intensifier but means flowering: the plural is both garden flowers related to pansies and stringed instruments

explanation.surface: Praise for some really excellent instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' seems slangy praise, but means flowering: the plants are pansy relatives, the instruments are lower than violins.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural names both flowering garden plants of the pansy family and the alto members of the string family.

clue.text: But testiness shouldn't characterize him

parts.note: testiness, read as test-iness, the quality of setting tests, does describe a tester, but a bad-tempered one is not wanted

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain official ought not to be irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: Testiness means irritability, but split as test-iness it fits someone who sets tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets and marks tests, such as an invigilator or assessor.

clue.text: Blake's tiger's was fearful

parts.note: a quotation from William Blake's poem The Tyger: 'Could frame thy fearful ...'

explanation.surface: A remark about the tiger in William Blake's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Blake's poem The Tyger ends its first verse with 'Could frame thy fearful symmetry?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blake's line speaks of the beast's balanced, matching proportions as fearful.

clue.text: Here trees supply mineral aggregates in small measure

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: ft is the abbreviation for foot, a short unit of length
ores are mineral deposits from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: A woodland is said to yield a little of its mineral wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is 'in'. 'Here trees' is the definition: a place where trees grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A large area covered in trees is a woodland of this kind.
